caseStudies.name: Genentech
caseStudies.dek: Redesigning and governing 30+ disconnected Genentech brand sites into one simplified, consistent web experience.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: 25% below prior year's costs; ~40% projected reduction in ongoing creative/production spend

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Lead UX Designer · Publicis Sapient · Sept 2021 – Feb 2022

Simplified Web Experience (SWE): redesigning and governing 30+ Genentech brand sites (cancer, MS, and other therapeutic areas) into one consistent, manageable system.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Genentech is a biotechnology company developing medicines for serious and life-threatening diseases, including the first targeted antibody for cancer. Feedback from patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers (HCPs) across Genentech's 30+ brand sites was consistent: the digital experience was disjointed and confusing. Content was organized around programs and campaigns instead of treatment; navigation language was inconsistent site to site; and the enrollment process for financial support programs was complex enough to delay patients from getting help. For HCPs supporting patients across multiple Genentech medications, that inconsistency compounded — every brand site worked a little differently.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Publicis Sapient hired me as Lead UX Designer on the SWE initiative. I owned implementation across the Genentech portfolio: auditing individual brand sites against the new standard, customizing the design system per brand where needed, running manuscript reviews and QA, and training each brand team (they're managed independently) on the SWE process. I also owned evaluating and improving that process as we scaled it across brands.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: Patients and caregivers needed treatment information organized around their actual decisions, not around Genentech's internal program structure. HCPs' frustration wasn't about any single site being bad — it was the inconsistency across sites when supporting patients on multiple medications. And the enrollment process itself, not just its design, was a barrier: financial support information and enrollment lacked consistency and clarity across brands, increasing both confusion and error.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Instead of a single top-down redesign imposed on every brand, SWE worked as a phased, co-created rollout: modular content built around user interests rather than campaigns, templatized design and navigation so brand teams weren't rebuilding patterns from scratch, and streamlined design/production processes so the system could actually scale to 30+ sites without a proportional increase in effort.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Interview synthesis, opportunity mapping, the SWE process model, and brand-level design system customization (color, buttons, navigation) from the Erivedge brand rollout.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: The 2021 investment came in 25% below the prior year's web creative and production costs, with a projected 40% reduction in ongoing annual costs as the modular system matured. Brands that launched under SWE saw increased customer satisfaction and decreased call center volume — and the initiative built the foundation for content modularity and personalization going forward.

caseStudies.name: Walgreens
caseStudies.dek: Standardizing design and implementation across Walgreens' fragmented digital ecosystem with a scalable, accessible design system.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Faster speed to market and improved cross-channel consistency across web and mobile app

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Associate Creative Director · Publicis Sapient · 12 weeks

Design system work to unify Walgreens' fragmented digital ecosystem across web and mobile.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Walgreens was operating with more than five disconnected design tools across its many lines of business, producing a fragmented digital ecosystem that was inconvenient for teams to work in and unreliable for customers using it.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led ACD-level design system work: setting the standardization strategy and directing the build of a scalable, atomic design system meant to work across every digital touchpoint Walgreens ships.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: The fragmentation wasn't just a design-consistency problem — disconnected tools meant no reliable single source of truth, which slowed implementation and made governance across teams close to impossible.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Built a scalable, flexible design system using atomic design principles to support rapid iteration; unified styles across web and mobile app for a consistent, optimized experience; comprehensive documentation to support adoption; integrated tooling for a single source of truth and streamlined governance; and accessibility-compliant components with documentation and annotations built in from the start, not bolted on after.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Design tokens, color and typography systems, light/dark mode, and component work including the coupon card pattern.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: The design system drove efficiencies in operationalization and implementation, faster speed to market, improved experience consistency across channels, and improved customer trust.

caseStudies.name: Mass General Brigham Health Plan
caseStudies.dek: Leading experience strategy for MGB Health Plan's HubSpot-to-AEM migration — steering it away from a lift-and-shift toward a genuinely redesigned, member-centered experience.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Future-state concepts across 10+ page types, grounded in 6 identified opportunity areas

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
XD Lead / Design Strategy Lead · Publicis Sapient · Sept 2023 – 2024

Leading experience design strategy for Mass General Brigham Health Plan's migration from HubSpot to Adobe Experience Manager, and the full redesign that came with it.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: MGBHP engaged Publicis Sapient to migrate their marketing website from HubSpot to AEM. The risk in any platform migration like this is treating it as a lift-and-shift — replatforming the same experience instead of using the migration as a forcing function to fix what wasn't working. My job was to make sure that didn't happen.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led experience design strategy across the full engagement, from discovery through future-state concepting: stakeholder interviews, competitive and comparative assessments, and a current-state analysis against the 2022 MGB Style Guide, followed by future-state design concepts across 10+ page types.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: The discovery work surfaced six distinct opportunity areas: simplified pathways to purchase, informed selection and comparison, a coherent "Member 360" view, clearer brand selection and transparency, transparent value and pricing, and advanced personalization. Each pointed to the same underlying issue — the existing site organized information around MGBHP's internal structure, not around the decisions members were actually trying to make.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Rather than migrate the existing site's structure into AEM as-is, I led future-state concepting across 10+ page types — home, plan finder, Medicare Advantage, plan comparison, blog, and navigation — each addressing one or more of the six opportunity areas. I also established a visual design library in Figma and surfaced design system gaps the AEM migration would need to account for, so the platform change and the experience redesign moved together instead of the platform work outrunning the design work.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: TK — Figma design library and future-state concepts are internal to the engagement; select screens to be added once cleared for portfolio use.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Positioned MGBHP to move beyond a lift-and-shift migration toward a genuinely redesigned, member-centered digital experience — with a concrete opportunity framework and 10+ page-type concepts to execute against.

caseStudies.name: Elevance Health
caseStudies.dek: Applying the same enterprise design system mandate from Walgreens to Elevance Health, one of the largest US health insurers.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Standardized design and implementation across multiple platforms and business lines

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Associate Creative Director · Publicis Sapient · 12 weeks

A parallel engagement to the Walgreens design system work, applied to Elevance Health (formerly Anthem), one of the largest health insurance providers in the US.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Elevance Health needed the same kind of standardization Walgreens did: multiple platforms and business lines running without a shared design foundation, making consistency and governance difficult at enterprise scale.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Directed the same ACD-level design system mandate applied at Walgreens, adapted to Elevance's platforms and business lines.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: Running this engagement in parallel with Walgreens surfaced a pattern: the same fragmentation problem — disconnected tools, no single source of truth — shows up across healthcare-adjacent enterprises regardless of whether they're a pharmacy or an insurer, suggesting it's a systemic issue in how these organizations scale digital products, not a one-off.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Standardized design and implementation across Elevance's platforms and business lines: a scalable design system, unified styles, accessibility compliance, documentation, and integrated tooling for a single source of truth — the same foundation as Walgreens, adapted to Elevance's specific platform constraints.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: TK — detailed visual documentation not yet migrated from the prior portfolio; pair conceptually with the Walgreens case study's design system artifacts.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Standardized design and implementation across Elevance's platforms and business lines, giving the organization a consistent foundation for future digital work.

caseStudies.name: PVH (Calvin Klein / Tommy Hilfiger)
caseStudies.dek: Standardizing Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, and PVH's other brand sites onto one CMS and design system without flattening what makes each brand distinct.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Unified CMS + design system across PVH's brand portfolio

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Associate Creative Director · Publicis Sapient · 8 months

Multi-brand design system migrating Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, and PVH's other properties onto a shared CMS and design system.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: PVH Corp. owns Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, and several licensed brands, each running on separate platforms with separate design conventions. An early undertaking was to standardize and migrate all brand sites to one common platform — PVH wanted a shared CMS with a consistent design system to gain efficiency across content, technology, and design, without losing what made each brand distinct to its audience.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led ACD-level design system work across the PVH brand portfolio: setting the systemization strategy, defining where brands could share a foundation versus needing brand-specific flexibility, and guiding the migration plan brand by brand.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: TK — full research writeup pending; the core tension the team navigated was efficiency (one shared system) vs. brand distinctiveness (Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger have very different visual languages).

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Rather than force every brand into identical templates, the system was built with a shared technical and component foundation but brand-level theming — so Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger could each keep their own visual identity while inheriting the same underlying CMS and component logic.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: See the Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger live sites, linked below.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body:
Realized efficiencies across content, technology, and design while improving UX consistency across devices and brands.

[View Calvin Klein site](https://www.calvinklein.us/) · [View Tommy Hilfiger site](https://usa.tommy.com/en)

caseStudies.name: BIO One-on-One Partnering
caseStudies.dek: Designing BIO's owned B2B partnering platform end-to-end as they moved off a vendor-managed system.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Full end-to-end partner discovery, scheduling, and meeting management experience

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Creative Director · Publicis Sapient · 2022

End-to-end platform design for BIO's One-on-One Partnering™ system, as BIO moved from a vendor-managed platform to one they fully own.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: BIO's One-on-One Partnering™ platform helps life science companies, investors, and researchers find and schedule meetings with potential partners. BIO wanted to internalize the platform — moving off a vendor-managed system to a fully owned, customizable, cloud-based product — to get greater control, better quality assurance, faster response times, and a better user experience than the vendor platform could offer.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led CD-level experience design for the internalized platform, owning the end-to-end partner discovery, scheduling, and meeting management experience.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: Because the platform serves a genuinely mixed audience — public pharma companies, biotech startups, academic researchers, non-profits, government, and investors — the core design challenge wasn't any single flow, it was making discovery and scheduling work for very different mental models of "finding a partner" without fragmenting the product into audience-specific versions.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Designed the discovery, scheduling, and meeting management flows as one connected system rather than separate tools, so a user could move from finding a potential partner to booking time with them without switching context or losing their place.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Platform screens covering partner discovery and meeting scheduling/management.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Delivered a fully owned, cloud-based B2B partnering platform — giving BIO the control and customization a vendor-managed system couldn't, and demonstrating ownership of a product's full lifecycle from strategy through design.

caseStudies.name: Johnson Financial Group
caseStudies.dek: Leading a multi-year digital transformation to merge Johnson Financial Group's siloed banking, wealth, and insurance experiences.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Increased customer engagement across business lines; decreased call center volume

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
UX Director · Verndale · January 2018 – March 2021

Multi-year digital transformation for Johnson Financial Group, a privately held financial services company spanning banking, wealth, and insurance.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: JFG was operating on an outdated, overly rigid CMS that made site maintenance and growth genuinely difficult. Their business lines were siloed from each other, creating a disconnect between marketing and data — and, from the customer's side, a fragmented experience depending on which JFG product they were using.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led UX for the multi-year engagement: directing the strategy for a user-centric, multi-channel experience and overseeing its execution across banking, wealth, and insurance.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: The siloed business lines weren't just an internal org problem — customers felt it directly, encountering inconsistent navigation, search, and content depending on which part of JFG they were interacting with, even though they thought of JFG as one company.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Designed a user-centric, multi-channel experience built around taxonomy-driven navigation and self-service features rather than JFG's internal business-line structure; added personalized content and revenue-optimized conversion paths; and implemented Episerver Personalization to support it.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Site design and navigation work spanning JFG's banking, wealth, and insurance experiences.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Increased customer engagement across business lines and decreased call center volume, as the taxonomy-driven navigation and self-service features gave customers a way to find what they needed without calling in.

caseStudies.name: Acadian Asset Management
caseStudies.dek: Designing a bold new digital identity for a systematic investment manager repositioning itself as digital-first.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Distinctive digital design system balancing brand personality with consistency

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Lead UX Designer · Verndale · January 2021 – July 2021

New digital identity and site redesign for Acadian Asset Management, a global systematic investment manager repositioning as digital-first.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Acadian wanted to reposition itself as a different kind of asset manager — one with a distinctive perspective in a market where most competitors look and sound the same. That meant a digital-first approach to reimagining their brand identity, not just a visual refresh.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Partnered directly with Acadian to design the new digital identity: transforming the site into an artful expression of the brand, implementing intuitive navigation, and applying accessible, inclusive design practices without dulling the brand's bold, creative spirit.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: The tension to resolve wasn't accessibility vs. boldness — it was proving those two things aren't actually in conflict. A financial brand can be expressive and still be usable and inclusive; treating accessibility as a constraint on creativity would have undersold both.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Built the color palette around patterns in nature, echoing Acadian's business of finding patterns in financial markets — sophisticated, unexpected, and forward-looking rather than typical finance-brand blue. Used angles and lines as a graphical device that complements the logo, kept flexible and abstract enough to hold up across digital contexts. Customized a geometric sans-serif for headlines to carry the same gestural confidence as the linework, and stripped back unnecessary elements so the core brand elements could do the expressive work.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Brand expression, navigation, and full-site design work reflecting the nature-inspired palette and typography system.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Delivered a bold, distinctive digital design system that balances brand personality with consistency — every touchpoint unmistakably Acadian, without sacrificing accessibility.

caseStudies.name: Sunrise Senior Living
caseStudies.dek: Rebuilding the digital foundation for a 35-year senior living brand through competitive research and structured IA work.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Competitive analysis across 6 competitors informed a full IA and navigation redesign

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Lead UX Architect · Verndale · January 2021 – July 2021

Digital transformation for Sunrise Senior Living, the fifth-largest senior living provider in the US, spanning 320+ communities.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Sunrise had a 35-year legacy as an innovator in senior living, but their digital presence hadn't kept pace. To stay ahead of a rapidly evolving industry, they needed a solid digital foundation and a reimagined customer-facing web experience that could unlock growth in key markets.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led UX architecture for the transformation: directing the research, design, and development of a new public-facing SunriseSeniorLiving.com.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: A competitive analysis across six main competitors showed Sunrise lagging in specific, fixable areas: web accessibility, galleries and virtual tours, site navigation and overall IA, resources, thought leadership content, and the community pages themselves — not a broad "everything is behind," but a clear, prioritizable list.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Used persona-driven design paired with remote navigation testing (Treejack) and moderated user testing to redesign the site's IA and navigation — validating structural decisions with real users before committing to a rebuild, rather than relying on internal assumptions about how prospective residents and families actually look for a community.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Competitive audit and IA documentation from the Treejack navigation testing.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Gave a 35-year legacy brand a validated digital foundation to build on — with specific, research-backed direction on accessibility, navigation, and content gaps rather than a guess-and-check redesign.

caseStudies.name: ATCC
caseStudies.dek: Recovering a failed B2B ecommerce redesign for the world's leading biological materials supplier through incremental, rationale-driven design system work.
caseStudies.outcomeHeadline: Recovered a stalled redesign through incremental, evidence-based design decisions

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Lead UX Designer · Verndale · Oct 2019 – Aug 2020

B2B ecommerce recovery for ATCC, the world's leading supplier of biological materials to the life sciences community.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: A previous agency had failed to deliver a working ecommerce redesign for ATCC. Verndale was brought in not to start over, but to recover the engagement: analyze what had already been built, identify the gaps, and recoup as much of the client's initial investment as possible.

sections.heading: Your Role
sections.body: Led UX on the recovery effort — auditing the prior agency's incomplete work, identifying what was salvageable, and building the rationale needed to justify each subsequent design change to a client who had already been burned once.

sections.heading: Key Insights
sections.body: Because trust had already been damaged by the failed first attempt, the biggest constraint wasn't design quality — it was stakeholder confidence. Every proposed change needed a clear, defensible rationale before the client would approve it.

sections.heading: Design Decisions
sections.body: Rather than propose a fresh redesign, changes were made incrementally against the existing design system, each one tied back to a specific usability or technical gap identified in the audit — trading a faster "clean slate" approach for one that rebuilt trust step by step.

sections.heading: Visual Evidence
sections.body: Product listing, product detail, and mobile views from the recovered ecommerce experience.

sections.heading: Outcome & Impact
sections.body: Delivered a coherent B2B ecommerce UX despite complex stakeholder constraints and a damaged starting trust position — recouping value from a previously failed engagement.

content.home.hero.headline: I shape the vision, strategy, and experiences that help businesses reinvent themselves.
content.home.hero.subhead: Nathan Walsh — Creative Director, Publicis Sapient, embedded at Optum. Building unified, intelligent healthcare experiences at the intersection of AI, strategy, and product design.
content.about.positioning: I am an associate creative director and experience strategist at the intersection of AI, healthcare, and product design. As an Associate Creative Director at Publicis Sapient embedded within Optum (UnitedHealth Group), I help organizations move beyond surface-level modernization to build unified, intelligent experiences that put design at the center of the product lifecycle. My work on OptumRx's BenefitCentral platform and Optimus Assistant proves what's possible when experience leads strategy.
content.about.bio: Innovative UX and Creative Design Leader with over a decade of experience delivering transformative solutions in healthcare and retail. Expert in shaping and executing strategic visions that elevate user engagement and drive measurable business outcomes. Passionate advocate for AI-driven innovation, with deep expertise in designing seamless end-to-end experiences.
